title: Model Hypothesis
tag: Hypothesis 2 of 2 · for you to pass or correct
h1: The model: two designs to build, train on the cards and compare
lead: Nothing was built, trained or downloaded for this. It is the argued plan for the two models, their training on the three rented cards and the comparison between them. It stands on the data hypothesis, which you have not passed yet.
reached: This was run as a graph of thoughts, in the open: a plan fixed before the first thought, and every thought recorded with what it was made from, its score and its fate. The figures below are read from that record, not from memory.
steps: Eight tests and thirteen vetoes, and the plan of the search, both fixed before the first thought.
24 separate runs, each from a different starting point and blind to the others, plus 9 of my own earlier notes. Every option scored; two or three kept per part.
Four runs each combined kept parts into one model. All four scored on seven tests and every veto. None fell under a veto.
Two designs had no test below open. Each got one improvement pass at the points its score named.
14 options from six runs, two kept of each. Two runs wrote the whole pipeline; one was chosen and one cut in it removed.
The search's own check passes. All 61 entries of the learning notes on models are used in a decision.

designs.name: Record, trees, reader
designs.start: Started from computing everything exact first
designs.verdict: Left standing. Trees read the exact record; a tuned reader corrects the top of the list. Lacks a learned propagation over typed links.

designs.name: Graph rooted at the question
designs.verdict: Left standing. Sums along typed links from the question's own files, each earlier change weighed by what it was about. Lacks trees and the depth of A's reader.

designs.name: Cascade under a large code model
designs.start: Started from a large tuned language model
designs.verdict: Ordered below, not vetoed. Its way of reaching far files had no route for a file tied only by a longer chain of links or by similar earlier work.

designs.name: Graph over a large code model
designs.start: Started from a language model inside the graph
designs.verdict: Ordered below for the same reason. By its own count the large model's pass over all content left room for only a small one.

limits: Every thought was read once and scored by me, against a yardstick I wrote. No design can be checked exactly before it is trained.
The runs were given the yardstick, so their agreement on what it demands is not independent proof.

I departed from my own plan twelve times, each on record: two pauses at the usage meter, three cards in place of four, thoughts over their word limits, three selections made in words where the levels tied, one improvement pass run although my stop rule already held, a final change of my own that I scored myself, and the written hypothesis put together by a script so that its record section is word for word.
For 16 of the 84 thoughts written by runs, the check could not confirm the writer from the transcripts.
This cannot prove a design right. It gives the two best-argued ones and the predictions that can fail.
